text: {"frames":["The windmill sails in the Tower have stopped, and flour dust hangs in the air like frozen snow. Olive, who keeps the forgotten things on the top floor, climbs down the ladder with a lantern in her hand. Yesterday there was no mill hall here at all, and now a wide floor of oak planks stretches over the canal. The miller needs to know how many square metres the floor covers before he can order enough linseed oil for the drying racks. Which of these is the size of the mill hall floor, in square metres?","Creak, creak, comes from the Tower's lowest floor, like a rope pulled tight on a barge. Briony the old lock keeper rows her flat boat up the canal and finds a new chamber of water where the wall used to be. The gate beams are rotten and the canal is leaking into the mill hall below. Briony needs to know how much floor the hall covers so she can count the sandbags for the dyke. Which of these is the size of the mill hall floor, in square metres?","Pieter throws his skates onto the frozen canal and glares at the footprints that come out of nowhere and stop at the water's edge. Anke sits on the windmill steps with her arms folded and says the mill hall is bigger than the cheese market. They argue about it until the ice starts to crack under their feet. Nobody can settle the quarrel without knowing how many square metres the mill hall floor really covers. Which of these is the size of the mill hall floor, in square metres?","Have you seen my shadow anywhere on the dyke, Teun asks the watchman, who never sleeps and never speaks. The watchman points at a chalk line on the floor of the mill hall, drawn in the wrong place by a careless apprentice. Teun kneels and measures the floor with his wooden clogs, but his count keeps coming out different. He needs the right size of the mill hall floor, in square metres, before the tulip festival tomorrow. Which of these is the size of the mill hall floor, in square metres?","The stork lands on the cheese scale in the middle of the Tower and asks for a number in a voice like rustling reeds. Flora the talking stork has been asked to judge who measured the mill hall floor best. Three cheese makers have given their answers, and the fog drifts between them as if it is listening. The stork will only believe the answer that matches the true size of the floor, in square metres. Which of these is the size of the mill hall floor, in square metres?"]}
